Package gov.cdc.izgateway.security

Class ServerSslBundleReloader

java.lang.Object
gov.cdc.izgateway.security.ServerSslBundleReloader
@Component public class ServerSslBundleReloader extends Object
Rebuilds and pushes the embedded HTTPS listener's named SslBundle when its backing keystore/truststore file changes on disk, by polling file modification time rather than relying on Spring Boot's own reload-on-update (inotify-based WatchService).

Inotify does not reliably detect a change written by a different client to a network filesystem -- confirmed for this application's actual deployment, where the keystore lives on an AWS EFS (NFSv4.1) volume (IGDD-3582). Polling file mtime is the same, already-proven-correct mechanism this library already uses for the outbound client TLS path (ClientTlsSupport/KeyStoreLoader).

This class only provides the check-and-reload operation; deciding how often (or whether) to run it is left to the consuming application -- see ServerSslBundleReloadScheduler in izgw-hub -- since polling cadence is a deployment policy decision, not something a shared library should dictate to every consumer.

  • Constructor Details

    • ServerSslBundleReloader

      public ServerSslBundleReloader(@Autowired org.springframework.boot.ssl.SslBundleRegistry sslBundleRegistry, @Autowired org.springframework.boot.ssl.SslBundles sslBundles, @Autowired org.springframework.core.env.Environment environment, @Autowired org.springframework.core.io.ResourceLoader resourceLoader)
      Create the reloader.
      Parameters:
      sslBundleRegistry - The application's SSL bundle registry, used to push a rebuilt bundle. Spring Boot registers one bean implementing both this and SslBundles.
      sslBundles - The application's SSL bundles, used to look up the current bundle (to preserve its key/options/protocol across a reload).
      environment - The application's environment, used to resolve server.ssl.bundle and the named bundle's spring.ssl.bundle.jks.* properties.
      resourceLoader - The resource loader used to resolve keystore/truststore locations, consistent with how Spring Boot's own bundle registrar resolves them.

  • Method Details

    • reloadIfChanged

      public void reloadIfChanged()
      Checks whether the configured bundle's keystore/truststore files have changed since the last call (or startup), and if so, rebuilds the bundle from disk and pushes it into the registry. No-ops when server.ssl.bundle is not configured -- legacy, non-bundle SSL configuration has no reload path, by design.
